title: The right adjoint for a finite etale morphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,V$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $e:V\to X$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the module direct image $e_*$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] is exact. Its total derived functor [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is computed termwise, and there is an adjunction on the entire, possibly unbounded, derived categories:
$$
Re_*=e_*:D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\rightleftarrows D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):e^*,\qquad e_*\dashv e^*.
$$
Here $e^*$ is the exact inverse image, applied termwise [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For the compact-support assertion, additionally use the ambient setting of the source unit: $X,V$ are finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and $e$ is a $k$-morphism. For compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], use the proper compactification $c=(\operatorname{id}_V,e)$. With this choice on the entire derived category,
$$
Re_!^{c}=Re_*=e_*\dashv e^*.
$$
On the subcategory where compactification independence has been established, this is the usual identification $Re_!=Re_*$.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf-level reverse adjunction [lem-sf-finite-etale-proetale-reverse-adjunction] with R = ULift A. Conjugate it by sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence on V and X. The normalized sfIntrinsicDirectImageComparison from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] identifies the left functor with the actual intrinsic direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]; its right functor is sfIntrinsicPullback. The intrinsic direct image already preserves finite limits, and its new left adjunction supplies finite colimits. This proves exactness without imposing boundedness or constructibility.

Use the exact-functor construction [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The library rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies RF with the exact termwise derived functor, and mapDerivedCategoryFactors identifies Q followed by RF with the degreewise functor followed by Q, proving the displayed isomorphism for [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The proved mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction derives the transported adjunction. Apply the exactness comparison on the right and its inverse on the left to obtain RF left adjoint to the specified termwise inverse image [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Finite implies proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so Compactification.ofIsProper has open part the identity. Identity extension by zero is the identity: its adjunction has right adjoint upperStar id, naturally isomorphic to the identity, so uniqueness of left adjoints gives the required isomorphism. Conjugate it by the scalar realization and descend it termwise. Whiskering with RF identifies the intrinsic compact-support functor [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] with RF. In the finite-field clause, l distinct from the prime characteristic is a unit in the finite field, hence in its algebraic closure and every stalk of a scheme over it. Apply the first theorem and transport its left adjoint along the compact-support isomorphism. This proves the clause on the entire derived category without compactification independence.
